description: On 19 June 2024 Public Safety Minister Dominic LeBlanc announced the IRGC was listed as a terrorist entity under the Criminal Code, effective that day.

IRPA s.34(1)(f) makes a person inadmissible on security grounds for being a member of an organisation there are reasonable grounds to believe engages in terrorism. A finding can rest on an admission, documents or service records.
energy_note: Your own honest answer on a form becomes the evidence.

description: In Vadiati the Court held conscript service could establish membership for s.34(1)(f), following the established approach that membership does not require ideological commitment or involvement in any specific act.
notes: Verify Vadiati directly (Federal Court) before citing - this is a practitioner summary.

description: In July 2024 the Minister amended the start date of the Iranian regime designation to 23 June 2003, so senior officials who served at any time since then may be barred, and those already in Canada investigated and removed.
energy_note: A rule written in 2024 reaching back twenty-one years.

description: Men who did compulsory service and were assigned to the Sepah may receive a Procedural Fairness Letter questioning admissibility - the first many hear of it, often years into an application.
money_note: Legal representation to answer the PFL.

aspect: The government says it is individual; an MP says otherwise
description: IRCC states that 'membership in the IRGC and service in the IRGC are distinct considerations' and that applications are assessed individually. In November Canada said it does not automatically reject PR applications solely for compulsory service - after a conscript said he had been ruled inadmissible for involuntary service.
energy_note: Reassurance issued only after the thing it denies had happened.

description: MP Garnett Genuis said the government failed to protect those forced into conscription - 'We shouldn't be punishing victims of forced conscription' - and proposed targeting instead those who volunteered, stayed on, or committed atrocities, suggesting a legislative exemption as the fastest fix.

aspect: The defence got weaker, not stronger
description: A practitioner guide notes 'the honest picture changed in 2025', with older defensive arguments having weakened - so a man whose case was arguable in 2024 may not be arguable now.
energy_note: The ground moving under a case already filed.

aspect: SCENARIO - the two years he cannot explain away
description: Omid served 2019-21. His unit was a Basij-affiliated logistics depot outside Karaj; he drove a truck and did inventory. In 2025 IRCC sends a procedural fairness letter asking him to address possible inadmissibility under s.34(1)(f). He is asked to prove a negative about an assignment he was given at nineteen by a lottery.
energy_note: Asked to disprove a posting you never chose.
